# Odunayo Blessing Adesina

> Odunayo Blessing Adesina is an environmental scientist and PhD researcher working on algal-bacterial bioremediation, nutrient recovery, and emerging contaminants.

Odunayo Blessing Adesina is a Nigerian researcher. She is a PhD researcher at the Institute of Soil Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences. She is completing an M.Sc. in Environmental Science at Tongji University through the UNEP-Tongji Institute of Environment for Sustainable Development (IESD).

Her work focuses on ecology and bioremediation for pollution and climate change, including biological nutrient removal, energy recovery, herbicide degradation, and the effects of emerging contaminants on microbial communities and ecosystem health.

Tagline: Restoring ecosystems through microbial innovation.

## Affiliations

- PhD: Institute of Soil Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences
- M.Sc.: UNEP-Tongji Institute of Environment for Sustainable Development (IESD), Tongji University, Shanghai, China
- B.Sc.: Microbiology, Institut Superieur de Communication d'Organisation et de Management (ISCOM) University, Benin Republic

## Research Focus

- Algal-bacterial consortia
- Biological nutrient removal and wastewater treatment
- Emerging contaminants, including antibiotics and herbicides
- Soil bioremediation and microbial community change
- Climate action through bioremediation and nutrient recovery

## Education

- PhD researcher, Institute of Soil Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences. Focus: bioremediation of herbicide-contaminated environments using algal-bacterial consortia.
- M.Sc. Environmental Science, Tongji University (UNEP-Tongji IESD). GPA 4.56 out of 5.0. Dissertation: Enhanced Nutrient and Antibiotic Removal in Algal-Bacterial Biofilm Reactors for Treating Ammonium-rich Wastewater. Advisor: Prof. Wang Rongchang. Chinese Government Scholarship (China Scholarship Council).
- B.Sc. Microbiology, ISCOM University, Benin Republic. GPA 3.67 out of 5.0.

## Publications

Peer-reviewed publications from 2024 to 2026 include work in Science of The Total Environment, Biodiversity (Taylor and Francis), Aquatic Ecology, and related journals. Manuscripts under review cover soil bacterial community change in bioremediation and coupled herbicide biodegradation and nitrogen fixation by algal-bacterial consortia in paddy fields.
